notes.summary: Software is the set of programs that tell the hardware what to do. Tier 2 asks 2–4 questions on types of software, operating system functions and terms, and language translators.

concepts.title: Types of software
concepts.body:
• System software: runs the computer itself. Examples: operating system, device drivers, BIOS/firmware, utilities (antivirus, disk defragmenter), language translators.
  • Application software: does a user task. Examples: MS Word, Excel, Tally, Photoshop, web browsers.
  • Open source: source code is free to see and change (Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox). Proprietary: owned by a company (Windows, MS Office). Freeware is free to use; shareware is free for a trial period.

concepts.title: Operating system
concepts.body:
The OS manages memory, processes, files and devices, and gives the user an interface (CLI like MS-DOS, or GUI like Windows).
  • Booting: loading the OS from disk into RAM. Cold boot = from power off; warm boot = restart.
  • Multitasking: many tasks at once for one user. Multiprogramming: many programs kept in memory. Time-sharing: CPU time split among users.
  • Virtual memory: uses part of the hard disk as if it were RAM.
  • Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line): jobs (e.g. printing) are queued on disk.

concepts.title: Language translators
concepts.body:
TranslatorConvertsHow
CompilerHigh-level → machine codeWhole program at once
InterpreterHigh-level → machine codeLine by line
AssemblerAssembly → machine codeMnemonics to binary
Machine language (0s and 1s) is the 1st generation; assembly is the 2nd; high-level languages (C, Java, Python) are the 3rd.

varieties.name: Types of software
varieties.how: Ask: does it run the computer (system) or do a user job (application)? Then check the licence type.

example.q: Is a device driver system software or application software?
steps: A driver lets the OS talk to hardware.
It runs the computer, not a user task.

varieties.name: Operating system terms
varieties.how: Match the term to its one-line meaning: booting, multitasking, virtual memory, spooling, GUI.

steps: Cold boot starts the computer from power off.
Warm boot restarts a computer that is already on (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+Del / Restart).

varieties.name: Languages and translators
varieties.how: Compiler = whole program, interpreter = line by line, assembler = assembly language.

example.q: Which translator shows errors one line at a time and stops at the first error?
steps: An interpreter executes one line at a time.
So it stops as soon as a line has an error.

tips: Linux, Android, Windows, macOS, iOS, Unix and MS-DOS are operating systems; MS Excel and Oracle Database are not.
Android is based on the Linux kernel.
Files deleted in Windows go to the Recycle Bin; Shift+Delete removes them permanently.
traps: A compiler is not faster to translate, but the compiled program runs faster than interpreted code.
Antivirus is utility (system) software, not application software, in most SSC keys.
Freeware is not the same as open source: freeware may hide its source code.

questions.q: Which of the following is system software?
questions.solution: The operating system manages the hardware and runs the computer, so it is system software. The others do user tasks and are application software.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an operating system?
questions.solution: MS Excel is a spreadsheet application. Linux, Windows 11 and Android are operating systems.

questions.q: A translator that converts the whole high-level program into machine code in one go is called a(n):
questions.solution: A compiler translates the entire program at once. An interpreter goes line by line; an assembler converts assembly language.

questions.q: The small program that starts the computer and checks the hardware, stored in ROM, is the:
questions.solution: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is firmware in ROM. It runs the POST check and then loads the operating system into RAM.
An assembler translates assembly language mnemonics (like ADD, MOV) into machine code (binary).

questions.q: In operating systems, SPOOL stands for:
questions.solution: SPOOL = Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line. Jobs such as print jobs are stored on disk in a queue and sent to the slow device one by one.

questions.q: Which of the following is open-source software?
questions.solution: LibreOffice's source code is freely available and can be changed. MS Office, Photoshop and Windows are proprietary.

questions.q: Virtual memory lets a computer use part of the ___ as an extension of RAM.
questions.solution: Virtual memory uses space on secondary storage (hard disk / SSD), called the page file or swap space, as if it were extra RAM.

flashcards.back: System software runs the computer (OS, drivers, utilities); application software does user tasks (Word, Excel, Tally).
Compiler: whole program at once. Interpreter: line by line.
Loading the operating system into RAM. Cold boot = from off; warm boot = restart.
Part of the hard disk used as an extension of RAM
The core of the operating system that controls hardware, memory and processes
Software free for a trial period; then you must pay
